subject: Frostline surge attenuation and throughput windowing — qualification & next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Doshi <samir@frostline.com>
Cc: Imani Brooks <imani@frostline.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Frostline: post-demo recap + throughput/latency asks

Hi Samir / Imani —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the data points we need to move the sizing forward so Marissa and Karthik can produce a baseline Dedicated/DXL config: 

Summary of what I heard you say (please correct):
- Primary use: conversational customer support assistant, hybrid chat + short tool calls (lookups).
- Latency target: 90th percentile <= 400ms per token for interactive chat (goal); 95th <= 700ms for peak windows acceptable with fallbacks.
- Typical steady-state: ~85 QPS across the fleet during business hours (~09:00–18:00 local).
- Peak windows: short spikes ~2–3x lasting 60–180s at the moment of batch releases.
- Tokens per request: median ~220 tokens generated, 95th ~900 tokens (rare long sessions).
- Streaming sessions: ~25% of requests use server-sent streaming; concurrent streaming sessions typically 40–60 during steady-state, up to 200 at peaks.

What we need from you to size properly:
1) A representative CSV export of 72 hours of traffic with timestamps, request type (chat/lookup), request tokens (input/output), streaming flag. If possible include session durations for streaming. (I attached a sample CSV template.)
2) Clarify whether those peak 2–3x spikes are correlated to scheduled events (deploy, campaign) or user-driven bursts.
3) Any hard limits on burst tolerance vs dropped/queued requests.

Next steps:
- If you can share the 72h export, Marissa will run throughput arithmetic and Karthik will correlate latency SLOs to feasible batch sizes and GPU choices.
- Tentative follow-up (30m): Nov 5 at 10:00 PT to review initial sizing.

Attachments: Frostline_sample_traffic.csv (template), Frostline_streaming-session-examples.txt

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0189

---
Note: If you prefer we measure in tokens/sec instead of QPS for the model mix, say the word and we will include both metrics in the sizing doc.

From: Samir Doshi <samir@frostline.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Frostline: post-demo recap + throughput/latency asks

Hi Grace — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications below: 

Correct: latency goals are as you summarized. A couple of items to call out:
- The spikes are mostly campaign-driven and happen when nightly digest emails hit customers (roughly 02:00–02:30 local) and when we bulk-release policy changes (ad hoc). We can annotate the 72h export with event markers.
- Tokens per request: median ~220 output, but input + output combined median ~480 tokens per API call (we often send a short context + history). Please size using total tokens per call.
- Streaming: when a session is streaming, average generated tokens streamed is ~180 and average session length is 12s. Concurrency numbers you have are right for steady state — peaks approach 240 streaming sessions for new releases.

I attached a 72h snip (anonymized) to this thread — Frostline_72h_export.csv. It contains timestamps, total_tokens, streaming_flag, request_type. 

Also: we have a hard SLA internally that critical customer-facing flows should not exceed 500ms P90. We can accept graceful degradation (smaller model fallback) for non-critical lookups.

Happy to hop on Nov 5 at 10:00 PT to review the sizing outputs.

— Samir
Samir Doshi
Head of Platform Engineering, Frostline Logistics
samir@frostline.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Doshi <samir@frostline.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Frostline: post-demo recap + throughput/latency asks — data landed

Marissa / Karthik –

Forwarding the 72h export from Frostline (attached by Samir). Key asks summarized: size for total_tokens per call, support P90 <= 400ms for interactive chat ideally but acknowledging internal critical SLA P90 <= 500ms; streaming concurrency steady 40–60, peaks ~240. Spikes are campaign-scheduled and last 60–180s.

Please do two things before our Nov 5 check-in: 
- Marissa: run a first-pass arithmetic: compute tokens/sec and peak tokens/sec during their 5 largest spikes, and produce both QPS and tokens/sec baselines for a recommended Dedicated capacity band (min/target/burst). Put raw numbers + assumptions in a short table.
- Karthik: propose the model profile(s) and batch windows we should test in the microbenchmark (quantization, KV cache sizing, streaming worker concurrency). If feasible, include an initial GPU recommendation and an expected P90 latency range for the target configs.

I expect we will propose a canary config that keeps 20% headroom on peak tokens/sec and a fallback variant for extreme peaks.

Thanks — Grace

(attachment forwarded: Frostline_72h_export.csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 07:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FW: Frostline: post-demo recap + throughput/latency asks — initial sizing

Quick first-pass from the 72h sample (raw math, conservative):
- Observed steady-state median total_tokens/sec: ~18,600 tokens/sec across the fleet (equates to ~38 QPS at median ~480 tokens/call).
- Largest 3 spikes in the window: 2.8x, 3.1x, 2.6x over baseline; peak tokens/sec observed ~65,000.
- If we target 20% headroom on peak: sizing target tokens/sec = 78,000 tokens/sec.

Recommended starting Dedicated config:
- Baseline: 4x A100-80GB equiv nodes running optimized LLM runtime with 8 concurrent streams per GPU; expected P90 latency ~320–420ms (depends on batching).
- Canary (target): 6x A100-80GB equiv nodes for peak handling and rolling updates.
- Fallback path: smaller quantized variant (8-bit quant) hosted on cheaper nodes to reduce P90 to ~450–600ms under extreme load.

Action items before Nov 5 call:
- Karthik to run microbench scenarios enumerating batching windows (8–64 token windows) and streaming concurrency to produce a latency curve.
- I'll prepare a short spreadsheet with tokens/sec -> node count mapping and include assumptions (batch limits, KV cache hit %, streaming penalty).

I'll join the Nov 5 call with an initial graphic.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
